heuristic_statement: Dual-Track Lineage and Executable Verification Heuristic (DT-LEV): 1. Separation of Epistemological Layers: Historical facts (verbatim commits, code diffs, logs, file presence) must remain distinct from semantic interpretations (inferred intent, requirement meaning, evaluation claims); truth decisions regarding active requirement status must strictly derive from cited facts through explicit interpretive arguments. 2. Orthogonality of Lifecycle and Implementation: Requirement lifecycle status (Active vs. Superseded vs. Partially Superseded) is orthogonal to implementation state (Implemented, Partial, Unimplemented, Unenforced). A requirement superseded by a subsequent user instruction creates zero present corrective work regardless of whether it was ever implemented historically. 3. Normative Implementation Target: The normative target consists solely of active, surviving user requirements. Current machine behavior must be established strictly from executable runtime source code, deterministic workflow definitions, active configuration files, and persisted structural behaviors—never inferred merely from specification documents (e.g., Agents.md), filenames, or model self-reports. 4. Corrective Gap Principle: An outstanding defect constitutes actionable present corrective work if and only if the underlying user requirement survives active today and today's executable machine fails to deterministically implement or enforce it.
decomposition_rationale: To prevent context ceiling violations and token quota exhaustion while ensuring exhaustive coverage, the audit is decomposed into 21 focused, strictly sequential subquestions partitioned across five independent evidence domains: (1) Current Executable Machine Architecture and Runtime Enforcement; (2) Current Normative Specifications, Approval Rulebooks, and Step 3 Contracts; (3) Retired Evaluation Specifications and Routing Metadata; (4) Historical Requirement Lineage and Component Evolution from Git logs and patch records; and (5) Empirical Nonce Execution Runs (split granularly across 12 focused subquestions to keep every single subquestion context well below the 250,000-byte manifest ceiling). Two final synthesis subquestions perform rigorous supersession analysis, requirement lineage reconciliation, and completeness checks proving that every historical instruction and persisted nonce container is fully accounted for without sampling.

interpretation_requirements: Perform explicit completeness checks proving that every supplied nonce container in the archive manifest (including large runs tracked via commit lineage and metadata) has been accounted for.

completeness_strategy: Strict Manifest Size Verification: Every subquestion context is verified to remain well under the 250,000-byte manifest ceiling (maximum context across all subquestions is 228,944 bytes), eliminating any possibility of model context overflow or quota exhaustion.

No-Sampling Nonce Coverage: Every single persisted nonce run directory from the manifest is explicitly assigned to a targeted subquestion (step0_raw_fail_20260930T1325_2, step0_raw_fail_20260930_3, step0_raw_fail_20260930_4, step0_raw_fail_20260930T132500, agents_schema_migration_20260930_1, work_action_approval_rulebook_20260930_1, ground_truth_verification_skill_20260930_1, demo_20260930T155153_eadd5e5248, live_ground_truth_integration_20261001_1, role_separation_20260930T181400, merge_step3_tsr_evaluation_heuristic_20261001_1, skill_interface_20260930T155700, skill_reeval_20260930T170100, skill_revision_20260930T180700, skill_revision_schema_reject_20260930T181100), with skill_bootstrap_update_20260930T170700 verified through its commit lineage log and audit data metadata.

Exhaustive Historical Lineage Tracking: Full chronological Git lineage and individual component patch logs are traversed to extract every relevant user prompt and instruction from the initial commit through the head commit.

Three-Tier Epistemological Auditing: For every requirement and supersession decision, sub-evaluators must produce a traceable dependency chain: Raw Facts -> Semantic Interpretations -> Truth Decisions.

Executable Source Grounding: Specification text in Agents.md is treated purely as stated intent; true machine behavior is established solely by parsing executable Node.js logic in send-to-gemini.js and GitHub Actions workflows in gemini-chat.yml and dependency sync definitions.

Orthogonal Lifecycle Reconciliation: All historical requirements are cross-classified by requirement lifecycle (Active vs. Superseded vs. Partially Superseded) and runtime implementation state (Implemented vs. Partial vs. Unimplemented vs. Unenforced), ensuring only surviving active requirements with implementation deficiencies are flagged as present corrective work.
